problems.title: Recall and quality crisis: record 152 NHTSA recalls in 2025
problems.problem: Ford issued a record 152 safety recalls in 2025 — the most by any automaker in a single year, nearly double GM's prior record of 77 in 2014 — spanning parking modules that allow rollaways, fire-risk electrical faults, and detaching parts (CBT News, Jan 2026). About 40 of those recalls were reissued software updates after audits found gaps in how OTA installations were verified. Ford doubled its safety team and expanded software validation over two years, and it told investors warranty costs are finally declining, but the volume of field failures is still forcing dealership service bottlenecks and holding some new vehicles undeliverable.
problems.why_data_team: Ford's Quality organization and the Integrated Services / software analytics teams own this; defect discovery now runs through connected-vehicle telemetry, warranty claims, dealer repair notes, and software audit logs — all data-heavy systems where early-warning models and pipeline reliability determine how fast Ford catches defects before they become headlines.
problems.solution: Build a defect early-warning platform that fuses connected-vehicle telemetry, warranty claims, dealer free-text repair data, and supplier part-lot genealogy into one pipeline, then scores every VIN and part lot daily for failure propensity using gradient-boosted survival/classification models. Add NLP/RAG over repair narratives to classify emerging failure modes and cluster complaints into candidate defect signals, plus automated reconciliation that verifies OTA update success rates to catch the 40-recall reissue pattern. A weekly 'recall risk leaderboard' by program, plant, and supplier would let engineering act before NHTSA thresholds are hit.
bottlenecks: Warranty claims and dealer repair narratives arrive with weeks-to-months lag and inconsistent free-text coding, weakening early signal
Telemetry, warranty, supplier, and software-audit data live in separate systems with different VIN keying, making joins lossy
Attribution across part lots requires supplier genealogy data Ford does not fully control
Recall decisions carry legal and regulator-reporting constraints, so models can only advise, not auto-trigger, actions
problems.mimansa_connection: Mimansa's 70M+ event ETL pipeline and LightGBM model (0.72–0.74 AUC, 25x targeting lift) is exactly the pattern needed to score millions of VINs for defect propensity off noisy warranty and telemetry data.
problems.booth_question: With 152 recalls last year, how is the quality analytics team using connected-vehicle telemetry and dealer repair text for early defect detection, and where do data engineering versus data science responsibilities sit in that pipeline?

problems.title: Supply-chain fragility: F-150 line halts and the Novelis aluminum fallout
problems.problem: A supplier component shortage halted F-150 production at Ford's Dearborn Truck Plant for roughly a week starting Sept 24, 2026, idling the Kansas City F-150 plant too, and CEO Jim Farley confirmed it will dent Q3 2026 wholesale truck deliveries (Quartz/Yahoo Finance, Sept 30, 2026; Detroit Free Press, Sept 25, 2026). This compounds the September and November 2025 fires at the Novelis aluminum plant in Oswego, NY: Ford absorbed roughly $800M in charges in the first half of 2025 alone, the disruption is expected to cost about $1.5B total, and F-Series sales were still down 11% through August 2026 as Ford tries to build 150,000 extra trucks to recover.
problems.why_data_team: Ford's Supply Chain and Enterprise Analytics organizations own supplier risk, inventory, and production planning; the F-150 is Ford's profit engine, so even short line stoppages are a forecasting, visibility, and optimization problem across multi-tier supplier, logistics, and plant data.
problems.solution: Stand up an end-to-end supplier risk and disruption analytics product: consolidate internal procurement, plant inventory, logistics, and quality data with external signals (supplier financial health, weather, facility events, port congestion) into automated DAG pipelines, then use graph analytics to map multi-tier dependencies and flag single points of failure like the Novelis aluminum site. Layer ML models for component shortage probability and days-of-supply forecasting, and run scenario simulation of plant shutdown/recovery to recommend buffer inventory and alternate sourcing before lines stop. Dynamic re-planning models can also reallocate scarce components across Dearborn, Kansas City, and Kentucky to protect the highest-margin mix.
bottlenecks: Tier-2/Tier-3 suppliers don't share capacity, inventory, or business-continuity data, so visibility stops at Tier 1
Key inputs like aluminum were effectively single-sourced, so there is no fast alternate supply even when the risk is known
Production re-planning has to run on short cycles (days) against long lead times and union/labor constraints
External disruption signals are noisy, and false alarms erode trust in the model with planners
problems.mimansa_connection: Mimansa's automated DAG pipelines consolidating 40+ sources is directly applicable to fusing procurement, plant, logistics, and external disruption feeds into one supplier-risk data layer.
problems.booth_question: After the Novelis fires and the recent F-150 supplier shortage, how far down Ford's supplier tiers does risk data actually reach, and what would a successful supplier early-warning data product need to prove to planners?

problems.title: EV losses and tariff exposure forcing a capital-allocation pivot
problems.problem: Ford posted an $11.1B Q4 2025 net loss — its largest quarterly loss since 2008 — after losing $4.8B on EVs in 2025, and it projects $4B–$4.5B more EV losses in 2026 while targeting break-even only in 2029 (NY Post/Fox Business, Feb 11, 2026). In December 2025 Ford took a $19.5B charge on EV assets and its product roadmap as it cut F-150 Lightning production and refocused on hybrids and a $30,000 EV platform; separately, tariffs cost roughly $2B in 2025 (including an unplanned $900M hit from a retroactivity change) and are expected to stay near that level in 2026. Full-year EBIT of $6.8B narrowly missed the revised $7B guidance even as Q4 revenue of $45.9B beat expectations.
problems.why_data_team: Ford's Finance/Strategy analytics, Ford Pro and Model e business teams, and Enterprise Data & AI own the unit-economics, demand-forecasting, and scenario models that guide where capital goes — this is fundamentally an analytics problem of measuring true per-vehicle profitability and forecasting demand by powertrain under policy uncertainty.
problems.solution: Build a powertrain-level profitability and scenario platform: a per-model, per-vehicle contribution-margin model that decomposes material, tariff, battery, warranty, and incentive costs from transactional and BOM data — the analytics equivalent of a DCF per vehicle line. Layer demand forecasting that segments EV vs hybrid vs ICE by region, incentive environment, and tax-credit status, and run Monte Carlo tariff/regulatory scenarios to produce decision-ready ranges for capital allocation, similar to how a churn model prioritizes retention spend. Automated pipelines refreshing these models weekly would replace static annual planning assumptions with continuously updated capital-allocation signals.
bottlenecks: EV demand and policy (tax credits, tariffs, retroactivity rules) shift faster than traditional annual planning cycles
Per-vehicle cost data is fragmented across BOM, supplier contracts, warranty, and segment accounting, making true unit economics hard to observe
$19.5B in written-down EV assets creates organizational resistance to models that might recommend further cuts
Tariff and regulatory rules change with little notice, so models need fast re-parameterization and transparent assumptions to be trusted by finance
problems.mimansa_connection: Mimansa's $75M ARR churn model shows she can translate messy behavioral/financial data into quantified dollar impact, and her DCF financial modeling maps directly to building EV unit-economics and tariff scenario models.
problems.booth_question: As Ford realigns its EV roadmap, which analytics output has the most credibility in capital-allocation debates — per-vehicle contribution-margin models or powertrain demand forecasting — and how does the data team handle fast-moving tariff assumptions?

problems.title: Cost inflation eroding the operating ratio despite 7% volume growth
problems.problem: In Q2 2026 BNSF's revenue rose 15% to $6.6 billion and volume rose 7% to 2.5 million units, yet its operating ratio worsened by 0.6 points as operating expenses jumped 16% to $4.3 billion, led by a 68% surge in fuel expense to $1.2 billion and a 2% rise in compensation and benefits to $1.4 billion from wage inflation (Progressive Railroading, Aug 10, 2026, citing BNSF's Q2 2026 quarterly financial performance review). BNSF has budgeted $3.6 billion of 2026 capital investment, down from $3.8 billion in 2025, with $2.8 billion earmarked for maintenance including 13,000 miles of surfacing, 2.5 million rail ties and 400+ miles of rail (Progressive Railroading, Jan 27, 2026). Moving more freight while unit costs rise is a classic productivity and cost-attribution analytics gap heading into the career fair.
problems.why_data_team: BNSF's operations, finance and service-performance analytics teams own cost-to-serve, fuel efficiency and crew-productivity reporting; explaining OR variance requires joining waybill, locomotive telemetry, fuel and payroll data at scale, which is inherently a data engineering and modeling problem.
problems.solution: Build a cost-driver attribution pipeline that joins train-level fuel burn, locomotive telemetry, tonnage and crew data to decompose operating-ratio variance by corridor and commodity, then use gradient-boosted models to forecast opex and flag anomalies before they hit the quarter. Layer a fuel-efficiency predictor (train makeup, horsepower-per-ton, weather, speed) specifically at the +68% fuel line, plus a crew-productivity and dwell dashboard to protect the compensation line. Orchestrate it as scheduled DAGs with data-quality checks so finance and operations see the same numbers.
bottlenecks: Fuel price volatility is largely exogenous and hedged, limiting controllable levers
Locomotive and capex cycles (budget cut to $3.6B) constrain efficiency gains
Crew scheduling is governed by union agreements, restricting optimization headroom
Ops, finance, mechanical and fuel data live in siloed legacy systems
problems.mimansa_connection: Her 70M+ event ETL pipeline feeding a LightGBM model (0.72-0.74 AUC, 25x lift) is the same pattern needed for train-level cost-driver attribution and opex anomaly detection.
problems.booth_question: How does BNSF's analytics org currently decompose operating-ratio variance — is it still reporting-heavy, and where would a cost-attribution or anomaly-detection model create the most value?

problems.title: UP-NS merger threat demands competitive and regulatory analytics
problems.problem: Union Pacific's proposed $85 billion acquisition of Norfolk Southern would create the first transcontinental U.S. rail network (Reuters/CNBC coverage, July 2025). The Surface Transportation Board adopted a procedural schedule for the revised major merger application on Aug 18, 2026 and on Sept 18, 2026 denied motions seeking summary denial; BNSF filed a petition asking STB to enforce and review the 1990s Union Pacific/Southern Pacific merger conditions, and BNSF, CPKC and CSX are pressing for broad access to any combined UP-NS network. BNSF is running a public 'Preserve Rail Competition' campaign at bnsf.com/merger, and the STB has also been finalizing BNSF access terms elsewhere (e.g., Lake Charles, July 21, 2026).
problems.why_data_team: This is a strategic/market analytics problem owned by BNSF's planning, marketing and regulatory teams, which need traffic-flow, rate and network models to quantify competitive harm and justify access remedies in STB filings.
problems.solution: Stand up a merger-impact simulation: ingest STB waybill/carload data, BNSF revenue and interchange records, and build origin-destination diversion models to estimate which traffic, gateways and rates shift to a combined UP-NS under different access remedies. Add RAG over STB filings to track applicant commitments and precedent conditions, and expose scenario dashboards with DCF-style revenue impacts so leadership can argue for conditions with evidence. Orchestrate STB, shipper and internal sources into one repeatable evidence pipeline.
bottlenecks: Waybill and rate data are confidential, lagged and often sample-based
STB regulatory timelines are exogenous and move quickly
Legal, finance and network-planning data are siloed across departments
Access remedies are negotiated outcomes, not purely analytical outputs
problems.mimansa_connection: Her DCF/financial modeling plus RAG pipelines map directly to merger scenario modeling and extracting commitments from dense STB filings.
problems.booth_question: As the UP-NS proceeding moves through the STB, is BNSF building quantitative network-diversion models to support its case, and would analytics hires contribute?

problems.title: Coal volume down 8% as plant retirements and cheap gas accelerate the energy transition

Over the same quarter, consumer-products intermodal volume grew 9% to 1.6 million units and agricultural/energy volume grew 12%, so the railroad must forecast a major mix shift to redeploy locomotives, hopper cars and crews. BNSF's 2026 plan funds Barstow, Phoenix and yard expansions precisely to serve that growth.
problems.why_data_team: Demand forecasting sits with BNSF's marketing/planning analytics organization; forecasting coal by mine, utility and plant needs econometric and hierarchical models fed by EIA, customer and internal shipment data.
problems.solution: Build a plant-level coal-demand forecast that models utility burn using natural-gas price cointegration, retirement schedules and EIA data, then rolls up hierarchically to corridor and fleet decisions. Treat plant retirements like a churn problem (survival/hazard model) to predict timing risk, and couple the forecast to car/locomotive allocation and long-range capex scenarios so capacity can be redeployed toward intermodal lanes growing 9-12%. Automate the pipeline so forecasts refresh as gas prices and retirement announcements change.
bottlenecks: Natural-gas prices and EPA rules are exogenous shocks
Utility retirement plans shift with policy and data-center load growth
Long asset lives make capacity reallocation slow and capital-intensive
Customer/utility demand data is often contractual and lagged
problems.mimansa_connection: Her $75M ARR churn model and econometrics training translate directly to plant-retirement hazard modeling and gas-price-driven coal demand forecasting.
problems.booth_question: How does BNSF forecast coal demand decline by utility and plant, and does that forecasting sit with the analytics team or with marketing?

problems.title: Crane Clean Energy Center restart: permitting, water, and schedule risk on a 2027 deadline

Outputs feed trading desk hedging and long-term contract pricing.
